Thank you, President Klein.
Thank you, Dean Bates, Dean Palaro.
Congratulations to the class of 2026.
Congratulations also to all the parents, the grandparents, the brothers, the sisters, and all of the family and friends who have been with the graduates through their journeys.
There is nothing more valuable than meaningful relationships.
Please give each other an enthusiastic round of applause.

谢谢克莱恩校长。
谢谢贝茨院长、帕拉罗院长。
祝贺2026届的同学们。
同时也祝贺所有的父母、祖父母、兄弟姐妹，以及所有在这段旅程中陪伴毕业生们的家人和朋友。
没有什么比有意义的人际关系更宝贵的了。
请彼此报以热烈的掌声。

I'm thrilled to be your commencement speaker, because it's an opportunity for me to tell you, who I see as myself 55 years ago, what I've learned in the 55 years since I've graduated from LIU that, you know, hopefully will be of some help to you.
我很激动能担任你们的毕业典礼演讲嘉宾，因为这让我有机会告诉你们——你们就像55年前的我——从我毕业于长岛大学至今55年里所学到的东西，希望这些对你们有所帮助。

While I remember being where you are when I was 21 years old, graduating in 1971 from what was then called CW Post College, I don't remember who the commencement speaker was, or what he said, and I suspect that you won't remember that later in your lives, but all I remember was nursing a hangover from celebrating the hard night before, and being elated at graduating and reflecting on how hugely LIU had an impact on my life in improving my life.
我清楚地记得自己21岁时，1971年从当时的CW Post学院毕业，和你们现在一样。但我完全不记得当时的毕业演讲嘉宾是谁，也不记得他说了什么。我猜你们将来也会忘记这些。我只记得自己因为头天晚上狂欢庆祝而宿醉未醒，为毕业而欣喜若狂，并回想起长岛大学对我人生、对我改变人生的巨大影响。

You see, I got into LIU on probation because I was a lousy high school student with a rebellious nature.
I remember hating high school, because it seemed to me that most of my education consisted of teachers forcing me to memorize what they wanted me to remember, which included a lot of useless stuff, and it didn't help that I had a very bad rote memory.

你们看，我是以试读生身份进入长岛大学的，因为我在高中时成绩很差，而且天生叛逆。
我记得自己讨厌高中，因为在我看来，我的大部分教育就是老师强迫我记住他们想让我记住的东西，其中包含大量无用的内容，而且我的死记硬背能力非常差，这更是雪上加霜。

At the same time, I love playing markets.
Which is where my attentions went.
I got hooked on playing markets when I was 12 while working as a caddy at the Lynx Golf Club, which was not far from here.
The stock market was hot.
And the people I carried for would walk around with me, and we would talk about stocks.
So I took the money that I earned, and I put it in the stock market.
The first stock I bought was the only stock I heard of that was selling for less than $5 a share.
I thought I could buy more shares so that if they went up, I'd make more money, which was a dumb strategy.
The company that I bought was about to go bankrupt, but I got lucky.
Another company acquired it.
It tripled in value.
I thought this game is easy, and I became hooked on playing this investment game at 12.

与此同时，我喜欢做市场投资。
我的注意力都放在了这上面。
我12岁时在山猫高尔夫俱乐部当球童(那个俱乐部离这儿不远)，就在那时迷上了市场投资。
当时股市很火爆。
我为之服务的人会和我边走边聊股票。
于是我把挣来的钱投进了股市。
我买的第一只股票，是我听说过的唯一一只每股价格低于5美元的股票。
我当时想，我可以买更多股，这样如果股价上涨，我就能赚更多钱——这是个愚蠢的策略。
我买的那家公司当时濒临破产，但我运气好。
另一家公司收购了它。
它的价值翻了三倍。
我心想，这游戏太简单了。于是从12岁起，我就迷上了这个投资游戏。

So at the time when I came here, I hated school, and I love playing markets until I got into Post.
I loved being here because I could take classes that interested me and engage me in quality thinking.
And I did well.
And so I went on to Harvard Business School, which was another eye opening learning experience.

所以在我来到这里之前，我讨厌上学，热爱市场投资——直到我进入CW Post学院。
我喜欢在这里读书，因为我可以选修自己感兴趣的课程，这些课程让我投入高质量的思考。
而且我学得很好。
后来我去了哈佛商学院，那又是一次让我大开眼界的学习经历。

When I was 19 and a sophomore here, I learned something that I found even more powerful than my formal education.
The Beatles went to India to learn to meditate.
And they raved about it, so I learned to meditate, which has been invaluable to me.
Meditation gives you an equanimity, aligns your subconscious with your conscious mind, and it is also restful and healthy.
It also gives you a sense of spirituality.
What I mean by a sense of spirituality is connection to the whole.
You have a sense of connection of where you are within the context of the whole.

我19岁，在这里读大二的时候，学到了一样东西，我发现它比我接受的正式教育更强大。
甲壳虫乐队曾去印度学习冥想。
他们对此赞不绝口，于是我也学习了冥想，这对我而言价值不可估量。
冥想让你内心平静，让你的潜意识与显意识保持一致，而且它还能让人放松、有益健康。
它还会给你一种灵性层面的感受。
我所说的灵性感受，是指与整体的连接。
你会感受到自己在整个图景中所处的位置。

So as a graduation gift to those of you who want it, I'm going to give you lessons in transcendental meditation.
It is the most valuable gift that I can give anyone.

所以，作为毕业礼物，我将为那些想要学习超觉冥想的人提供课程。
这是我能给任何人最宝贵的礼物。

Over my 55 years since graduating, I've learned a lot about how life works and how to deal with it in order to be successful, including what being successful really is.
I learned that life is a journey of discovery, in which the goal is to understand your own nature and find the right path to suit you.
That, there is nothing more important than having good principles to guide you.
By principles, I mean, ways of handling certain situations.
Over my lifetime, I've accumulated hundreds of principles, which is far too many to cover in this 15 minutes that I have with you.
So I'm giving you also my book, Principles: Life and Work, which I hope will help you find the right principles for you, and to get what you want out of life.
You can find it below your seat, along with the card to sign up for the meditation.

在毕业后的55年里，我学到了很多关于生活如何运作、如何应对生活以获得成功(包括成功的真正含义是什么)的道理。
我认识到，生活是一段发现之旅，其目标是理解你自己的本性，并找到适合你的正确道路。
而且，没有什么比拥有正确的原则来指引你更重要的了。
我所说的原则，是指处理特定情况的方法。
在我的一生中，我积累了数百条原则，数量太多了，无法在这15分钟里全部讲完。
所以，我也把我的书《原则：生活与工作》送给你们，希望它能帮助你们找到适合自己的原则，并得到你们在人生中想要的东西。
你们可以在座位下面找到这本书，还有一张报名参加冥想课程的卡片。
I think I'm going to put this down and not struggle with it.
我想我还是把它放下，不用费力举着它了。

So it seems to me that you are about to travel along a similar life path, a similar arc in life to the one I've traveled on, and most people travel on, experiencing the same phases, and having many of the same encounters I had.
So I want to tell you what to expect and give you some tips.

在我看来，你们即将踏上的生命旅程，与我所走过的、大多数人所走过的人生轨迹相似，经历相同的阶段，遇到许多与我相似的境遇。
所以我想告诉你们将会遇到什么，并给你们一些建议。

Looking back on my and others' lives, I came to see that life unfolds in three big phases that are very different from each other.
In the first phase, you are learning and you're dependent on others.
In the second phase, you are working, and others are dependent on you.
And in the third phase, which is the phase where I am, you are free from obligations and able to pass along what you've learned.

回顾我自己和他人的人生，我发现生命会展开为三个大阶段，彼此非常不同。
在第一阶段，你处于学习期，依赖他人。
在第二阶段，你工作，他人依赖你。
在第三阶段——也就是我现在所处的阶段——你摆脱了义务，能够传递你所学到的东西。

The second phase, which you are about to enter, is more opposite than similar to the first.
Rather than being in an education program and having instructors, you will guide yourself to achieve your goals, and you will encounter thrilling opportunities and painful setbacks, which, if you reflect on well, will teach you what you want, what you're like, and how to be successful.
You will learn that thinking for yourself, making painful mistakes, and learning from them, and knowing how to deal with what you don't know is what is most valuable.

你们即将进入的第二阶段，与第一阶段相比，更多是对立而非相似。
你将不再是处于教育项目中、拥有老师指导，而是自己引导自己去实现目标。你会遇到激动人心的机会和痛苦的挫折——如果你能好好反思，这些经历会教会你：你想要什么、你是什么样的人、以及如何取得成功。
你会学到：独立思考、犯下痛苦的错误并从中学习、以及懂得如何处理自己不知道的东西——这些才是最有价值的。

In the early part of this second phase, which will be about your next 10 years, the most important thing for you is to experiment, and reflect well so that you discover your nature, and what is the path that is best for you.
在第二阶段的早期(大约是未来的10年)，对你们来说最重要的事情是去尝试、并好好反思，从而发现自己的本性，以及哪条路最适合你。

When entering this phase two, you are almost certainly making the mistake of thinking you know more than you actually know, especially if you got good grades in school.
You don't yet have a clue about what life is really like, and you don't yet know what being successful really means for you, let alone what to go after and how to get it.
You couldn't possibly know these things, because you haven't yet experienced or thought about what you will encounter.

在进入第二阶段时，你们几乎一定会犯一个错误：认为自己知道的比实际知道的多——尤其是如果你在学校里成绩还不错的话。
你们对生活真正的样子还一无所知，也还不知道成功对你们自己到底意味着什么，更不用说该追求什么以及如何实现了。
你们不可能知道这些事情，因为你们还没有经历或思考过自己将会遇到什么。

In the first phase, your teachers and parents typically led you to believe that success is a matter of learning what you were taught and not making mistakes.
And you were taught to take pride in what you know.
That probably made you a bit arrogant, like I was a bit arrogant when I graduated from here.

在第一阶段，你的老师和父母通常会让你相信：成功在于学习教给你的东西，并且不犯错误。
你被教育要为自己知道的东西感到自豪。
这也许让你变得有些自傲，就像我从这里毕业时也有点自傲一样。

But it is living life and encountering your realities that will teach you.
The question is, Will you learn well?

但真正起作用的，是去经历生活以及遭遇你自己的现实——这些才会教会你。
问题是：你能学好吗？

My nature and encounters with realities led me to become a professional investor, which led me to start an investment firm out of my two bedroom apartment.
While I ran it for 50 years, built it into the largest hedge fund in the world, and then passed it along to the next generation, which many people consider a great success story, I know that it was learning from my painful mistakes that made me successful.

我的本性和与现实经历的碰撞，让我成为了一名专业投资者，这又促使我从小小的两居室公寓里创办了一家投资公司。
虽然我经营了它50年，把它打造成世界上最大的对冲基金，然后把它交给下一代——很多人认为这是一个巨大的成功故事——但我知道，正是从痛苦错误中学习，才让我获得了成功。

For example, when I was 34 years old, and had run Bridgewater for eight years, I calculated that American banks had lent much more money to emerging countries than those countries were going to be able to pay back, and that that would lead to a great debt crisis, almost the largest since the Great Depression.
And it was a very controversial view.
But in August, 1982, Mexico defaulted on its debt, and a number of other countries followed, and we did have the greatest debt crisis since the Great Depression.
Because I had anticipated that, I was asked to testify to Congress and appear on Wall Street Week, which was the show at the time.

例如，在我34岁、已经经营桥水基金八年的时候，我推算美国银行借给新兴国家的钱，远远超过了这些国家的偿还能力，这将导致一场自大萧条以来几乎最严重的债务危机。
这是一个非常有争议的观点。
但在1982年8月，墨西哥对其债务违约，其他一些国家也相继违约，我们确实经历了一场自大萧条以来最严重的债务危机。
因为我曾预见到这一点，我被邀请到国会作证，并参加了当时一档名为《华尔街周刊》的节目。

I thought the stock market would fall a lot, but I couldn't have been more wrong.
The stock market and economy went up rather than down, and I lost so much money for myself and my clients that I had to let almost everybody go, and I was so broke that I had to borrow $4,000 from my dad to help pay for my family bills.

我当时认为股市会大幅下跌，但我大错特错了。
股市和经济不但没跌反而上涨，我为我自己和客户亏了很多钱，以至于不得不让几乎所有员工都离开，我破产到不得不从我父亲那里借了4000美元来支付家庭账单。

It was one of the most painful experiences of my life.
But it turned out to be one of the most valuable experiences of my life, because it gave me the humility I needed to balance with my audacity.
Rather than thinking, "I'm right," I thought about, "how do I know I'm right, and how do I find that out?"
That led me to find the smartest people who would disagree with me, to understand their perspectives, and have them stress test my own perspective.
It also led me to understand diversification, how I could reduce my risk without reducing my returns.
In other words, I learned from that.
From that point on, my company, Bridgewater, did very well, and I learned, and it did well, because what I learned, I never would have learned without that painful mistake.

那是我人生中最痛苦的经历之一。
但它后来变成了我人生中最宝贵的经历之一，因为它给了我所需的谦逊，来平衡我的大胆。
我不再想着"我是对的"，而是思考：我怎么知道我是对的？我怎样才能弄清楚这一点？
这让我去寻找那些会反对我的、最聪明的人，去理解他们的视角，并让他们对我的视角进行压力测试。
这也让我理解了多元化，明白了如何在不降低回报的情况下降低风险。
换句话说，我从那次经历中学习。
从那时起，我的公司桥水基金表现非常出色；我学到了东西，公司也因此发展得好，因为如果没有那次痛苦的错误，我永远也学不到那些东西。

My life journey also led me to meet and marry a wonderful woman, who I've been married to for 48 years.
It led me to have four children, which led me to have eight grandchildren who are the joys of my life.
Such is life.

我的人生旅程还让我遇到并娶了一位出色的女性，我与她结婚至今已有48年。
它让我有了四个孩子，又让我有了八个孙辈，他们是我生命中的快乐源泉。
人生就是这样。

I believe that the most important decision in your life will be who you choose as your life partner.
So that may be ahead, and that's an important decision.
For me and for everyone.
And will be true for you.

我相信，你人生中最重要的决定将是选择谁作为你的终生伴侣。
所以那可能还在前方，那是一个重要的决定。
对我如此，对每个人也是如此。
对你们也会如此。

There are lots of ups and downs along the way.
Some unimaginably great and some unimaginably terrible.
For example, I lost my son which was worse than losing everything, including my life.

一路上会有很多起起落落。
有些好得难以想象，有些糟得难以想象。
例如，我失去了我的儿子——这比失去一切(包括我自己的生命)还要痛苦。

What helped me through these challenges were two things:
My meditation and my calmly reflecting on how reality works to get and write down the best principles for dealing with my realities.
This habit changed my whole perspective on life.
I began to see almost everything as another one of those things which happened to many people before in their own ways, and knowing that there's a better way to deal with each one of those.

帮助我度过这些挑战的有两样东西：
我的冥想，以及我冷静地反思现实运作的规律，从而得出并写下应对我面临现实的最佳原则。
这个习惯改变了我整个人生观。
我开始把几乎所有事情都看作是"又一件那样的事"——很多人在我之前都曾以各自的方式经历过，而且我知道，每一类事情都有更好的应对方法。

One of my favorite principles that I learned through these sorts of experiences is: pain plus reflection equals progress.
I got in the habit of viewing pain as a signal that I have a problem, which I view as a puzzle to solve, that will give me a gem in the form of a great principle.
I learned to value my painful experiences, because they became my best learning experiences, and led me to make my best advances.

通过这些经历，我学到的一条最喜欢的法则是：痛苦加反思等于进步。
我养成了这样的习惯：把痛苦视为我有问题的信号，而这个问题就是一个需要解开的谜题，解开它就会给我一颗以伟大原则为形式的宝石。
我学会了珍视痛苦的经历，因为它们成了我最好的学习经历，并促使我取得了最好的进步。

I found that this approach to learning, from encounters with reality, to be a much better way of succeeding in life than remembering what others were trying to teach me.
Those experiences and making the most of them, especially the painful experiences are your opportunities.

我发现，这种从与现实遭遇中进行学习的方式，远比记住别人试图教给我的东西，更能让我在人生中获得成功。
那些经历——以及充分利用它们(尤其是痛苦的经历)——就是你的机会。

Remember that you were born with a certain nature.
And you are on your journey to understand it and find what suits you.
Knowing your nature is always critically important to helping you understand what success is for you.

记住，你天生具有某种本性。
而你正处在理解它、并找到适合自己的道路的旅程中。
了解自己的本性，对于帮助你理解成功对你意味着什么，始终至关重要。

People have different goals in life.
So I can't tell you, literally, what is best for you.
But I can tell you that success is not having a lot more money or status than you need, though most people think that that's what it is.
And, in fact, it can become an unhealthy obsession for a lot of people.
So avoid that.

人们在人生中有不同的目标。
所以我无法逐字逐句地告诉你什么对你最好。
但我可以告诉你，成功不是拥有远超过你所需的金钱或地位——尽管大多数人认为成功就是那样。
而且事实上，对很多人来说，这可能会变成一种不健康的执念。
所以要避免这一点。

Logically, having a lot more money than you need, couldn't possibly be a source of great happiness, compared with the alternatives.
For example, it isn't more important than having the time and freedom to do what you most want to do.

逻辑上来说，拥有远超过你所需的金钱，与其他事物相比，根本不可能是巨大幸福的来源。
例如，它并不比拥有时间和自由去做你最想做的事情更重要。

So, what do I believe success is for most people?
I believe that it is a matter of having meaningful work and meaningful relationships.
I'll say that again: meaningful work and meaningful relationships.
In other words, work and relationships that you are thrilled by.

那么，我相信对大多数人而言，成功是什么呢？
我相信，成功在于拥有有意义的工作和有意义的人际关系。
我再说一遍：有意义的工作和有意义的人际关系。
换句话说，是那些让你感到兴奋的工作和人际关系。

If you can make your work and your passion one and the same,
and you can do it with people who you care about and care about you, you will have a happy, successful life.

如果你能让你的工作和你的热爱合二为一，
并且你能和你所关心的、也关心你的人一起从事这份工作，你就会拥有幸福、成功的人生。

As you travel along on life's journey, you have a choice of your approach to life.
When life doesn't give you what you want, you can be angry or sad for yourself or you can learn about how reality works and develop principles that will work well to get you what you want.

当你在人生旅途中前行时，你可以选择自己的人生态度。
当生活没有给你想要的东西时，你可以为自己感到愤怒或悲伤，或者你可以去学习现实的运作规律，并制定出能够帮你得到你想要东西的原则。

I urge you to own your life and take responsibility to make it great.
Think about how reality works.
Be radically open minded to hear how you can be better and plan the moves to make, in order to improve your life and make yourself a great life.
And if you want to be really successful, recognize that you have to work damn hard at doing these things well.
Excellence is worth it.
That's just how life works.

我恳请你掌控自己的人生，并承担责任把它变得精彩。
思考现实是如何运作的。
保持极度开明的头脑，去听取如何让自己变得更好的建议，并规划出要采取的行动，从而改善你的人生，为自己创造精彩的人生。
而且如果你想真正成功，就要认识到你必须非常非常努力地把这些事情做好。
追求卓越是值得的。
生活就是这样运作的。

So the message that I want to leave with you today is that the most valuable thing you can have in the next phase of your life is not your diploma or even what you've learned thus far.
It is your approach to life.

所以，今天我想留给你们的讯息是：在你人生的下一个阶段，你能拥有的最有价值的东西，不是你的文凭，甚至不是你至今所学到的知识。
而是你的人生态度。

If you take advantage of your experiences, good or painful, as opportunities to learn, you will find great principles that will help you deal with your realities well.
In the process, you will discover your nature, and find excellent work and excellent relationships that will suit you, which will give you the best possible life.

如果你把自己的经历——无论美好还是痛苦——都当作学习的机会加以利用，你就会找到伟大的原则，帮助你妥善应对自己的现实。
在这个过程中，你会发现自己的本性，并找到适合你的卓越工作和卓越的人际关系，这将为你带来尽可能美好的人生。
So, class of 2026, congratulations, now get out there and encounter your realities, with your excellent sense of adventure.
所以，2026届的同学们，祝贺你们！现在走出去，去迎接你们的现实，带着你们卓越的冒险精神。
Thank you.
谢谢。

extra_quotes: Don't confuse goals with desires.
不要混淆目标与欲望。
A proper goal is something that you really need to achieve.
合理的目标是你真正需要实现的东西。
Desires are things that you want that can prevent you from reaching your goals.
欲望则是你想要但会阻止你实现目标的东西。
Typically, desires are first-order consequences.
通常来说，欲望是一阶后果。
For example, your goal might be physical fitness, while your desire is to eat good-tasting but unhealthy food.
例如，你的目标可能是身体健康，而你的欲望是吃美味但不健康的食物。
Don't get me wrong, if you want to be a couch potato, that's fine with me.
别误会我的意思，如果你想成为一个整天窝在沙发上看电视的人，我完全没问题。
You can pursue whatever goals you want.
你可以追求任何你想要的目标。
But if you don't want to be a couch potato, then you better not open that bag of chips.
但如果你不想成为那样的人，那你最好不要打开那包薯片。

extra_quotes: Comparing what is now happening with what has happened in analogous historical situations and triangulating my thinking with smart, well-informed leaders and experts has always helped me make better decisions. I have found that most wars are filled with big disagreements about what is likely to happen and big surprises. However, in the case of this Iran war, it is obvious, and there is near-universal agreement, that it all comes down to who controls the Strait of Hormuz. I hear from those who run governments, geopolitical experts, and people all over the world that if Iran is left with control over who can pass through the Strait of Hormuz, or is even left with the power to negotiate:

我常常对照历史上类似的事件研究眼下正在发生的事，也会反复与智慧高深、见多识广的领袖和专家“交叉验证”我的思路，一直以来，这让我的判断更准确、决策更高效。我发现，在绝大多数战争期间，大众对“接下来会发生什么”往往分歧巨大，而且战争期间总会发生一连串始料未及的突发事件。然而，这一次“美以袭击伊朗”的战事却不一样，大家几乎没有争议，都认为关键因素只有一个，就是看**谁能控制霍尔木兹海峡**。我从各国决策圈、地缘政治专家，以及来自世界各地的朋友那里，不断听到同一种说法：只要伊朗还拥有“谁能通过霍尔木兹海峡”的决定权，甚至哪怕伊朗还有拿这件事讨价还价的筹码，那么：

**1. The United States will be judged to have lost the war, and Iran will be judged to have won.** That is because Iran controlling the Strait of Hormuz to use as a weapon would be a clear demonstration that the U.S. does not have the power to fix this situation. The consequences of allowing Iran to shut down the most important strait in the world, through which the right of passage must be ensured at all costs, would be hugely damaging to the United States, its allies in the region (especially its Gulf allies), countries that depend most on its oil flow, the world economy, and the world order. If Donald Trump and the U.S. don't win this war—with victory being easily measured by whether they can ensure safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz—they also will be perceived to have caused a disastrous situation they could not fix. Whatever the reason that the United States doesn't win control of Hormuz—whether it is because anti-war politics threaten President Trump's political control ahead of the upcoming mid-term elections and he is afraid of that, because of his and the American electorate's lack of willingness to suffer the losses of lives and money required to win this war, because the U.S. doesn't have the military power to get and maintain control, or because he cannot bring together other countries in a consortium to keep this strait open—it doesn’t matter. President Trump and the U.S. will have lost.

**1. 在大家心中，这场战争就是伊朗获胜，而美国输了。** 原因在于：只要伊朗还把霍尔木兹海峡握在手里、能随时拿它当武器用，那就等于在全世界面前证明，美国没有把局面“收拾干净”的实力。霍尔木兹海峡是全球最关键的海峡，无论如何都要保障这条海峡畅通无阻。如果伊朗仍有能力随时关闭霍尔木兹海峡，必然会对美国、美国的中东盟友（尤其是海湾盟友）、最依赖海湾石油出口的国家、全球经济乃至世界秩序，造成极其沉重的打击。若特朗普和他的美国政府没能赢下这场战争，没有“显而易见”地保障霍尔木兹海峡安全通航，那么他们就是在全世界眼皮子底下，自己制造了战火和灾难，却没办法自己收场。美国为什么还没夺取霍尔木兹的控制权？可能是因为美国国内反战浪潮高涨，特朗普害怕在中期选举中失去对国会立法权的掌控；可能是因为特朗普本人和美国选民都不愿意为了这场战争牺牲美军生命和耗费美国财富；可能是因为美国现有军事实力根本不足以夺取海峡并长期防守控制；又或者因为特朗普没办法说服其他国家与美国联盟，一起维持海峡通航。但是，不管原因是什么，结论很明显：只要没有控制霍尔木兹海峡，特朗普和美国就是输了。

My reading of history and sense of what is now happening leads me to believe that if the U.S. were to lose in this way, there would be a significant risk that losing control of Hormuz would be for the United States what the Suez Canal Crisis was for Great Britain (in 1956) and analogous defeats were for the Dutch Empire in the 18th century and the Spanish empire in the 17th century. The pattern of events that leads to the breakdown of empires is almost always the same. While it is covered much more comprehensively in my book *Principles for Dealing with the Changing World Order*, I can tell you here that there are innumerable cases in which a perceived lesser power challenges the leading world power over the control of a critical trade route (e.g., Great Britain's control of the Suez Canal being challenged by Egypt). In these cases, the dominant power (e.g., Great Britain) threatens the lesser power (e.g., Egypt) to open the route, and everyone watches and shifts their approaches to these countries and where their money goes based on what happens. This decisive "final battle" that determines the winners and the losers and whether the empire survives or falls reshapes history because people and financial flows quickly and naturally run from the losers. These shifts affect markets, especially the debt, currency, and gold markets, and geopolitical power. Seeing so many analogous cases led me to the following principle: **When the world's dominant power that has the world's reserve currency is overextended financially, and it reveals its weakness by losing both military and financial control, watch out for allies and creditors losing confidence, the loss of its reserve currency status, the selling of its debt assets, and the weakening of its currency, especially relative to gold.**

借古鉴今，我越来越笃信：如果美国真的以这种方式输掉这场战争，那么今天的“霍尔木兹海峡危机”之于美国，很可能就像1956年苏伊士运河危机之于大英帝国，18世纪“第四次英荷战争”失败之于荷兰帝国、17世纪罗克鲁瓦战役惨败之于西班牙帝国，成为强大帝国走向衰败的转折点。导致帝国走向衰败崩解的历史事件，几乎是一个模子里刻出来的。虽然我在《原则：应对变化中的世界秩序》里做了系统阐述，但我还是想在本文重申：类似的历史案例简直数不胜数，通常是一个显而易见的弱国，在关键贸易通道的控制权上，公开挑战当时的世界头号霸主（比如当时埃及挑战英国对苏伊士运河的控制）。在对峙中，霸主（英国）威胁弱国（埃及）开放贸易通道；于是，世界各国密切关注事态发展，随机应变地调整自己对两边的态度和立场，调整资金要往哪里押。决定鹿死谁手、帝国延续还是崩塌的“终极决战”，必然会重塑历史走向，因为无论是人心还和金钱，都会天然地、迅速地远离输家，所谓“树倒猢狲散”。这种趋势会直接冲击市场，尤其是债券、汇率与黄金市场，同时也会重塑地缘政治力量格局。正是因为看过太多这样的历史事件，我才提炼出下面这条原则：**一个掌控国际储备货币的头号强国，如果在财政上过分负债、透支过度，又在军事与金融上失去控制地位，暴露出虚弱疲态，就要格外小心：盟友和债权人会对它失去信心，国际储备货币地位会动摇，债务资产会遭到抛售，本国货币会疲软，尤其是对黄金走弱（体现为本币计价的黄金价格走高）**。

Because people, countries, and financial flows quickly and naturally flock to the winner, if the U.S and President Trump don't get control of the flow of traffic through Hormuz, it will threaten American power in the world and the existing world order. While it was always assumed that the U.S. would be the dominant power and could win militarily and financially over its opponents (and certainly over its middling-power opponents), the cumulative effect of the military, financial, and geopolitical consequences of the wars in Vietnam, Afghanistan, Iraq, and perhaps this war with Iran, are not good for the United States and the sustainability of the post-1945, American-led world order.
Conversely, **when the world's dominant power demonstrates its military and financial strength, that bolsters confidence in it and the willingness to hold its debt and currency.** When President Reagan got the hostages in Iran released immediately after his election and then, when Iran attacked Gulf shipping during the Iran-Iraq War, President Reagan ordered U.S. Navy escorts for oil tankers, he demonstrated his and the United States' power over Iran. If President Trump demonstrates his and the U.S.'s power to do what he said he would do, which is win this war by having free passage through the Strait of Hormuz and eliminating Iran as a threat to its neighbors and the world, it will greatly bolster confidence in his and the U.S.’s power.

因为人心、国家立场与资本流向，都会自发迅速地向赢家靠拢；所以如果美国和特朗普无法夺取霍尔木兹海峡的控制权，无法保障航运通行，那么受到威胁的，就是美国的全球霸权和既有的世界秩序。过去，全世界都默认，美国作为头号强国，必然军事上打得赢，金融上也耗得起，所向披靡（那些“中等强国”更加不在话下）。但越南战争、阿富汗战争、伊拉克战争，再加上如今这场伊朗战争，在军事、财政与地缘政治上产生的后果，历历在目，深入人心，不仅让美国的形象日薄西山，也不断侵蚀着1945年战后那套“美国主导的世界秩序”。
反过来，**如果世界头号强国能展示出自己的军事与金融实力，那外界对它的信心就会随之抬升，也就更愿意继续持有它的国债与货币。** 回顾历史，里根总统刚刚当选，就迅速解救了在伊朗被挟持的人质；随后两伊战争期间，伊朗袭击海湾航运，里根下令美国海军为油轮提供护航，这些动作都在向伊朗展示：里根和美国有实力压过伊朗一头。同理，如果特朗普能兑现自己的承诺，“确保霍尔木兹海峡自由通航、并消除伊朗对周边国家地区与世界的威胁”，赢下这场战争，那么外界对特朗普及美国实力的信心，也会被大幅拉升。

**2. If, on the other hand, the Strait of Hormuz is left in the hands of the Iranians to use as a weapon to threaten American allies in the Gulf and the world economy more broadly, everyone will be hostage to the Iranians, and Donald Trump will be perceived to have picked a fight and lost.** He will have left U.S. allies in the region with a huge problem, and he will lose credibility, especially given what he has said. For example, Trump has said: “If for any reason mines were placed, and they are not removed forthwith, the military consequences to Iran will be at a level never seen before,” “we will take out easily destroyable targets that will make it virtually impossible for Iran to ever be built back, as a nation, again — Death, Fire, and Fury will reign upon them,” “the new leader in Iran will have to obtain our approval; otherwise, he will not last long.” I often hear senior policymakers in other countries say in private things like, “He talks a good game, but can he fight and win when the going gets tough?” Some observers are anticipating this fight like the Romans in the Colosseum or sports fans awaiting the final and greatest contests. President Trump is now calling on other countries to join the U.S. in ensuring the free passage through the Strait; his ability to get them to do so will be indicative of his ability to form alliances and muster power, so that would be a big win.

**2. 但是，如果霍尔木兹海峡仍在伊朗手里，伊朗还能利用它威胁海湾地区的美国盟友、乃至更广意的全球经济，那么所有人都会变成伊朗的“人质”。届时，外界会认为：特朗普先动手挑起了冲突，却打输了，玩砸了。美国的中东盟友要自己收拾一堆烂摊子；特朗普呢，前几天说过多狠的话，现在就要现多大的眼，信誉值受到暴击。** 比如，特朗普曾经放话：“要是（伊朗）胆敢（在霍尔木兹海峡）布设水雷，不把水雷马上清除干净，那伊朗就要面对史无前例的军事后果”；“我们会轻而易举地摧毁目标，让伊朗这个国家失去重建的可能，死亡、烈焰与怒火将排山倒海倾泻而至”；“伊朗的新领导人必须得到我们的批准，否则指日可die。”我常听到别国的高层决策者私下嘀咕：“特朗普嘴炮打得响，可真要打硬仗，他打得动、打得赢吗？”还有不少旁观者甚至把这场对决当成罗马斗兽场里的压轴戏，像观众一样等着看精彩的总决赛。此刻，特朗普正呼吁其他国家与美国一道，确保霍尔木兹海峡能自由通行；他能不能拉这些国家下场，本身就是对他“组建联盟、集结力量”能力的一次公开测验。如果他真能做到，那当然会是一场大胜。

It will be very difficult for the United States and Israel alone to ensure the safe passage of ships without prying Hormuz loose from Iranian control, and it will likely require a great battle to do so. The outcome is existential for the Iranian leaders and the largest and most powerful segment of Iran’s population. To the Iranians, this war is very much about revenge and commitment to what matters more than life. They are willing to die as a demonstrated willingness to die is essential for one's self-respect and showing the devotion that brings about the greatest reward—while Americans are worrying about high gas prices and America’s leaders are worrying about midterm elections. **In war, one’s ability to withstand pain is even more important than one’s ability to inflict pain.** The Iranians' plan is to try to drag the war out and steadily intensify it because it is widely known that the American public, and therefore American leaders, have very limited capacities for pain and wars that drag on. So, if this war is made painful enough and long enough, the Americans will abandon the fight and their Gulf "allies," and other "allies" around the world, will see that the United States will not be there to protect them. This will undermine the relationships with aligned countries in analogous situations.

如果不把霍尔木兹海峡从伊朗手里“撬出来”，美国和以色列想靠一己之力保障船只安全通行，必然难上加难；真要做到，打一场硬仗就在所难免。对伊朗的领导层以及伊朗庞大的权势阶级来说，这场战争，事关生死存亡。对伊朗百姓而言，这场战争很大程度上是复仇战，关乎他们“重于泰山”的信念和信仰。他们愿意为此赴死捐躯，因为“敢牺牲”本身就是自尊的底线，慷慨赴死能换来无上荣耀，而与此同时，美国百姓却在担心飙升的油价，美国的决策者在担心中期选举。**在战争中，忍辱负重不畏苦难，比心狠手辣更重要。** 伊朗的计划很清楚：尽可能把战争拖下去、并一步步升级烈度，因为众所周知，美国人民（因此也导致美国领导层）对“苦痛”的耐受上限很低，更受不了持久战。所以，只要把这场仗打得足够痛、打得足够久，美国人迟早会退缩撤离，抛下他们在海湾的“盟友”；而世界各地的其他“盟友”也会看得一清二楚：在关键时刻，美国不会保护他们的。这会从根本上削弱美国与同路国家之间的盟友关系。

**3. While there is talk of ending this war with an agreement, everyone knows that no agreement will resolve this war because agreements are worthless. Whatever happens next—i.e., leaving Hormuz in Iranian hands or taking control away from them—is likely to be the worst phase of the conflict. This "final battle," which will make crystal clear which side won and which side lost control, is likely to be a very big one.**
To quote Iran's military command, “All oil, economic, and energy facilities belonging to oil companies in the region that are partly owned by the United States or that cooperate with the United States will be immediately destroyed and reduced to ashes.” That will be what they attempt. If the Trump Administration is successful in its efforts to get other countries to join it in sending warships to provide safe escorts—and hasn’t already been mined—we will see if that becomes a solution. Both sides know that the final battle, which will make clear which side won and which side lost, still lies ahead. And they know that if President Trump and the United States don’t deliver on reopening the strait, it will be terrible for them. If, on the other hand, President Trump wins this final battle and eliminates the Iranian threat for at least the next several years, it will greatly impress everyone, empower President Trump, and demonstrate American power.

**3. 尽管外界议论纷纷，认为可以通过协议结束这场战争，但大家心里都清楚：靠协议结束不了这场战争，因为协议一文不值。接下来无论走势如何，不论是伊朗继续把霍尔木兹海峡攥在手里，还是美国从伊朗手里夺走控制权，都会是这场冲突最凶险的阶段。因为这场“终局之战”之后，谁赢得控制权、谁失去控制权，会清楚得不由分说，因此，这场“终局之战”将是一场恶战。**
伊朗军方发言人说：“本地区所有由美国持股或与美国合作的石油公司名下的石油、经济与能源设施，都会被立即摧毁，化为灰烬。”这就是他们接下来要干的事。如果霍尔木兹海峡还没布设水雷封死航线，如果特朗普政府真能拉其他国家下场，一起派军舰为商船护航，能不能化解这个危机就可以拭目以待了。双方都知道，真正的“终局之战”还在后头：到时“谁赢谁输”就会摊在阳光下。双方也都明白，如果特朗普和美国没能兑现承诺，没把霍尔木兹海峡重新打通，对他们来说会非常难看。反过来，如果特朗普真能赢下这场终局之战，或者至少在未来几年把伊朗的威胁压下去，则会让所有人刮目相看：特朗普的声势会水涨船高，美国也会再次证明自己的实力。

**4. The direct and indirect effects of this “final battle” will ripple around the world, affecting trade flows, capital flows, and geopolitical developments with China, Russia, North Korea, Cuba, Ukraine, Europe, India, Japan, etc.** The current war, along with other recent wars, is part of the far bigger classic Big Cycle progression that has financial, political, and technological implications. These implications can be best understood by studying past analogous wars and applying the lessons learned to current circumstances. For example, **a country’s financial and military capacities to fight wars are affected by the number and severity of the wars it is fighting, its internal politics, and its relationships with countries that have shared interests (e.g., between Iran, Russia, China, and North Korea)**. The United States doesn't have the capacity to fight multiple wars (no country does), and in a world that is so interconnected, wars, like pandemics, spread quickly in unimaginable ways. At the same time, within countries, especially within democracies that have great wealth and values differences, there is always fighting over what should be done and who should pay how much and in what form (i.e., money, lives lost, etc.). There will almost certainly be these sorts of direct and indirect relationships and consequences that are very difficult to anticipate but won't be good.

**4. 这场“终局之战”的直接影响与间接影响，会像涟漪一样扩散到全球各处：贸易流向会被改写，资本流向会重新站队，而围绕中国、俄罗斯、朝鲜、古巴、乌克兰、欧洲、印度、日本等一系列国家与地区的地缘政治演进，也会牵一发动全身。** 眼前这场战争，以及最近几年接连不断的其他战争，是更宏大的兴衰“大周期”里的一环，它在金融、政治与科技层面都有连锁反应。要理解这些后果，最可靠的办法，就是去找历史上相似的战争做对照，把当年总结出来的经验教训，映射到今天的处境上。比如，**一国的财政能力与军事实力，能不能打胜仗、能打多久，很大程度上取决于它同时卷入了多少场战争、战事有多惨烈；也取决于它的国内政治环境、与“利益一致”的国家结成了怎样的关系（例如伊朗、俄罗斯、中国与朝鲜之间的关系）**。美国没有能力同时打多场战争（任何国家都做不到）；而在这个高度互通互联的世界里，战争就像疫情一样，会以难以想象的方式快速外溢、蔓延。与此同时，在各国内部，尤其是在财富差异巨大、价值观分裂严重的民主国家里，争吵和攻讦绵延不休，该做什么事、该谁出钱、能付出多少的代价（花多少钱、牺牲多少生命），你争我吵，没有定论。可以肯定的是，错综复杂的直接与间接关联，以及由此引发的直接与间接后果，往往极难提前预判，大概率也不会是什么好消息。

To bring this note to an end, I want to emphasize that I am not political; I am just a practical person who has to bet on what will happen and has studied history to draw lessons that help me do that well, and I am now passing along my principles and thoughts that might help others navigate these tumultuous times. As I have explained before, from studying the rises and declines of empires and their reserve currencies over the last 500 years of history, which I did to help me make my global macro bets (and which I shared in my book and YouTube video *The Changing World Order*), **there are five big, interrelated forces that drive how monetary orders, political orders, and geopolitical orders come and go. They are: 1) the long-term debt cycle (comprehensively explained in my book *How Countries Go Broke: the Big Cycle*), 2) the related political cycle of order and disorder (that progresses in clearly identifiable stages and at its worst causes civil wars), 3) the related international geopolitical cycle of order and disorder (that also progresses in clearly identifiable stages and at its worst leads to devastating world wars), 4) the advancements of technologies (that can improve or destroy lives), and 5) acts of nature. What is now happening in the Middle East is just a small part of this Big Cycle at this current moment in time.**
**While it is impossible to anticipate and get all the details and specifics exactly right, it is quite easy to measure the health and the progressions of these five forces and the overall Big Cycle. The important thing for you to do is to ask yourself, is that Big Cycle progression true and are these indicators indicative of where we are in the Big Cycle—and if so, what should I do about it?** I remain ready, willing, and able to explore these things with you if you’d like to ask me questions in the comments.

写到这里，我想强调一句：我不热心政治也没有政治立场。我只是务实的人，本职工作需要我对未来“押注”，而我研究历史，就是为了从中提炼经验教训，让自己押得更准。现在，我把凝炼的原则和想法分享出来，希望能帮更多人穿越这段动荡时期。我之前介绍过，我研究了过去500年里各大帝国（朝代）及其储备货币的兴衰罔替，是为了辅助我做全球宏观押注（这些内容我写进了书里，也在视频《The Changing World Order》中讲过）。通过这些研究，我得出一个结论：**有五股彼此交织的力量，决定了货币秩序、政治秩序与地缘政治秩序的兴衰罔替。它们分别是：1）长期债务周期（我在新书《国家为什么会破产》里做了系统阐述）；2）与之相伴的国内政治“治乱”周期（有清晰明确的不同阶段，极端时会走向内战）；3）与之相伴的国际地缘政治“治乱”周期（同样有清晰明确的不同阶段，极端恶劣时会引爆毁灭性的世界大战）；4）技术进步（既能改善生活，也能摧毁生命）；5）大自然的力量。眼下中东正在发生的一切，只是这轮“大周期”在当下时点的一个小切面。**
**尽管不可能把所有细节和变量都猜中、一次性算得分毫不差，但要衡量这五股力量各自的“健康度”和演进速度，以及它们共同构成的“大周期”整体走到哪一步，其实并不难。真正该做的，是反问自己：这个大周期的推进逻辑，是不是真切的？这些指标，是不是能告诉我们当下正处于大周期的哪个阶段？如果“是”，那下一步我该怎么做？** 如果你愿意，欢迎在评论区提问，我愿意随时和你探讨这些问题。

瑞·达利欧 (Ray Dalio).content: 《2025年复盘与2026年预测》
extra_quotes: Naturally, as a systematic global macro investor leaving 2025, I reflected on the mechanics of what happened, particularly in the markets. That's what today's reflection is about.
作为一名在2025年离场的系统性全球宏观投资者，我自然而然地反思了这一年发生的内在机制，尤其是在市场层面。这就是我今天要分享的思考内容。
Though the facts and returns are indisputable, I see things differently from most others.
尽管事实和投资回报数据无可争议，但我的看法与大多数人截然不同。
In these reflections, I step back and look at how this money/debt/market/economy dynamic worked in 2025 and what that implies for 2026 and beyond.
在这些思考中，我退一步审视了2025年货币/债务/市场/经济的运行机制，以及这对2026年及未来意味着什么。

While most people think that U.S. stocks, particularly U.S. AI stocks, were the best investment and the story of 2025, I believe that the real story of 2025 was the collapse in the value of money and the shift away from U.S. assets.
大多数人认为美国股票，尤其是美国AI股票，是2025年最好的投资和年度核心故事，但我认为2025年的真正故事是货币价值的崩溃以及资本从美国资产的撤离。
There were two big drivers of returns that determined winners and losers: 1) what happened to the value of money, and 2) the relative performance of assets in different currencies.
有两个决定投资输赢的核心回报驱动因素：1) 货币价值的变化；2) 不同货币计价资产的相对表现。

Regarding 1) what happened to the value of money: the dollar fell by 0.3% against the yen, 4% against the renminbi, 12% against the euro, 13% against the Swiss franc, and 39% against gold (which is the second largest reserve currency and the only major non-fiat currency).
关于第一点，即货币价值的变化：美元兑日元下跌0.3%，兑人民币下跌4%，兑欧元下跌12%，兑瑞士法郎下跌13%，兑黄金（它是第二大储备货币，也是唯一的主要非法币货币）下跌39%。
So, all fiat currencies fell, and the biggest story and the biggest market moves of the year were the result of the weakest currencies falling the most and the strongest currencies holding up better.
因此，所有法定货币都在贬值，而今年最大的市场故事和最大的市场波动，正是源于最弱货币贬值幅度最大，最强货币相对保值的现象。

The best major investment of the year was long gold (returning 65% in dollar terms), which outperformed the S&P index (which returned 18% in dollars) by 47%. Or, said differently, the S&P fell by 28% in gold-money terms.
今年表现最佳的主要投资品是做多黄金（以美元计价回报率达65%），比标准普尔指数（以美元计价回报率18%）高出47个百分点。换句话说，以黄金计价的标准普尔指数实际上下跌了28%。
Let's remember some key principles that pertain to what is happening:
让我们记住一些与当前情况相关的关键原则：

When one's own currency goes down, it makes it look like the things measured in it went up. In other words, if your currency loses 39% of its value relative to gold, then things priced in that currency have to go up by 64% to have the same value in gold terms.
当本国货币贬值时，会让人感觉以该货币计价的资产价格上涨了。换句话说，如果你的货币相对黄金贬值39%，那么以该货币计价的资产价格必须上涨64%，才能保持与黄金相同的价值。
Regarding 2) the relative performance of assets in different currencies: non-U.S. stocks significantly outperformed U.S. stocks, and non-U.S. bonds significantly outperformed U.S. bonds.
关于第二点，即不同货币资产的相对表现：非美国股票显著跑赢美国股票，非美国债券显著跑赢美国债券。
Clearly, investors would have much rather been in non-U.S. stocks than in U.S. stocks, just as they would have much rather been in non-U.S. bonds than in U.S. bonds and cash dollars.
显然，相较于美国股票，投资者更愿意配置非美股资产；同理，相较于美国债券与美元现金，他们也更青睐非美债券资产。
This shift away from U.S. assets was not just about currency moves; it was also about the changing supply-demand picture for U.S. debt and the growing political risks.
这种撤离美国资产的趋势不仅与货币走势有关，还与美国债务的供需格局变化以及日益增长的政治风险有关。
The AI boom that powered U.S. tech stocks is now in the early stages of a bubble.
推动美国科技股上涨的人工智能热潮目前已步入泡沫初期阶段。
While AI is undoubtedly a revolutionary technology that will have a huge impact on all industries, the current pricing of AI-related assets reflects unrealistic expectations.
尽管人工智能无疑是一项将对所有行业产生巨大影响的革命性技术，但当前AI相关资产的定价反映了不切实际的预期。
Markets seem to have forgotten the lessons of past bubbles.
市场似乎忘记了过去几次泡沫的教训。
Looking ahead to 2026, the number one political issue will be the affordability issue—the "purchasing power of money" problem.
展望2026年，头号政治议题将是"可负担性危机"——即"货币购买力"问题。
The "haves" (who own assets) don't see inflation as a problem, while the majority (who don't own significant assets) feel overwhelmed by it.
"有产者"（拥有资产的人）不认为通胀是个问题，而大多数"无产者"（没有大量资产的人）则被通胀压得喘不过气。
This tension is setting up a big fight between the left and the right over wealth redistribution.
这种紧张关系正在引发左翼和右翼之间关于财富再分配的激烈斗争。

Based on historical relationships between yields, productivity, and profit growth, I estimate long-term expected equity returns at under 5% (specifically around 4.7%), which is extremely low by historical standards.
根据收益率、生产力和利润增长之间的历史关系，我估计长期预期股票回报率低于5%（具体约为4.7%），按历史标准衡量这一水平极低。
For 2026, my framework points to modest returns, higher volatility, and increased sensitivity to interest rate changes.
对于2026年，我的分析框架显示投资回报将较为温和，波动性会更高，且资产对利率变化的敏感度会增加。
The newly appointed Fed chair and the FOMC will be biased to push nominal and real interest rates down.
新任命的美联储主席和联邦公开市场委员会（FOMC）将倾向于推动名义利率和实际利率下降。
Though this may support asset prices in the short term, such policies would be supportive to prices at the expense of currency value.
尽管这可能在短期内支撑资产价格，但此类政策是以牺牲货币价值为代价来支撑价格的。
The 2026 midterm elections will be a pivotal moment for the "internal order cycle"—I believe we are moving toward the sixth phase (civil war/revolution phase).
2026年中期选举将是"内部秩序周期"的关键时刻——我认为我们正朝着第六阶段（内战/革命阶段）迈进。
The probability of civil conflict in the U.S. is now 35%-40%, as state and federal governments, left and right, increasingly refuse to accept legal rulings.
美国发生内战的概率目前为35%-40%，因为州政府与联邦政府、左翼与右翼之间越来越多地拒绝接受法律裁决。

In summary, I believe that: debt/currency issues are the biggest drivers of markets and economies; the shift away from U.S. assets and dollar dominance will continue; gold and other hard assets will remain attractive; and political tensions will increase, leading to greater market volatility.
综上所述，我认为：债务/货币问题是市场和经济的最大驱动因素；撤离美国资产和美元主导地位的趋势将持续；黄金和其他硬资产将保持吸引力；政治紧张局势将加剧，导致市场波动更大。
Investors should focus on preserving purchasing power rather than chasing nominal returns.
投资者应专注于保值，而非追逐名义回报。

瑞·达利欧 (Ray Dalio).source: X（原Twitter）/ LinkedIn双平台同步首发；桥水官网及达利欧个人网站收录
瑞·达利欧 (Ray Dalio).background: 2026年1月26日在X（原Twitter）和LinkedIn双平台同步首发，桥水基金官网及达利欧个人网站随后收录。文章以大周期理论框架分析美国正从第五阶段（现有秩序崩塌前夕）迈向第六阶段（现有秩序彻底崩塌），涵盖财政破产与内战先行指标、贫富差距与阶级对抗、民粹主义与妖魔化、政治暴力与准军事组织、货币体系与全球货币周期、国内冲突向国际战争传导等核心议题，附三种未来情景推演（有序衰退/长期停滞/全面战争），以"合作共赢优于内战与战争"收尾。
瑞·达利欧 (Ray Dalio).content: 《货币、内战与国际战争、明尼阿波利斯及更多 —— 透视当下》
extra_quotes: Money, Civil War, International War, Minneapolis, and More — Looking Through the Lens

货币、内战与国际战争、明尼阿波利斯及更多 —— 透视当下
---
Most people are shocked by what's unfolding in the world right now. I'm not. I've seen this movie before.
大多数人对当前世界正在发生的一切感到震惊。但我并不震惊。我早已见证过相似的历史轨迹。
The recent killings of ICE protesters in Minneapolis exemplify escalating violence and state-federal tensions, signaling potential movement toward civil conflict.
近期明尼阿波利斯发生的移民与海关执法局抗议者遇袭身亡事件，直观体现了暴力冲突升级、州政府与联邦政府之间的矛盾加剧，预示着社会有滑向内部冲突的风险。

The world order last collapsed between 1930 and 1945, which led to the post-WWII monetary, domestic political, and international geopolitical orders that began in 1945—and we are now witnessing the breakdown of these orders.

世界秩序上一次崩塌发生在1930至1945年间，此后1945年确立了二战后的货币体系、国内政治格局与国际地缘秩序，而如今，我们正亲眼目睹这套秩序走向瓦解。
---

In this article, I draw on my book *Principles for Dealing with the Changing World Order* to explain that the U.S. is now on the brink of moving from Stage 5 (before the collapse of the existing order) to Stage 6 (collapse of the existing order) of the Big Cycle.
本文将结合我的著作《应对变化中的世界秩序》展开分析：美国目前正处在大周期的临界点，即将从第五阶段（现有秩序崩塌前夕）迈入第六阶段（现有秩序彻底崩塌）。
Stage 3 of the Big Cycle is a period of peace and prosperity with good debt and credit conditions, while Stage 4 is when overconsumption and decadence begin to lead to deteriorating conditions.
大周期第三阶段是和平繁荣期，债务与信贷环境整体健康；到了第四阶段，过度消费与社会奢靡之风开始滋生，整体环境逐步恶化。

Stage 5 is when class conflicts peak due to worsening fiscal conditions. The Big Cycle ultimately reaches its hardest and most painful stage—Stage 6—when the country runs out of money and terrible conflicts typically erupt in the form of revolutions or civil wars.

第五阶段，财政状况持续恶化，阶级矛盾走向顶峰。当国家财政彻底枯竭，大周期就会进入最艰难、最痛苦的第六阶段，革命或内战这类激烈冲突往往会集中爆发。
---

Through studying more than fifty civil wars and revolutions, I have found that the most reliable leading indicators of civil wars or revolutions are government fiscal bankruptcy and large wealth gaps.
我研究过五十余场内战与革命，发现预判内战或革命最可靠的两大先行指标，分别是政府财政破产与悬殊的贫富差距。

This is because when a government lacks fiscal strength, it cannot bail out the private sector entities necessary to keep the system running (as most governments, especially the U.S., did in late 2008), it cannot buy needed goods, and it cannot pay people to do what it needs done. It loses power.
原因在于，一旦政府失去财政能力，就无力救助维系社会运转的私营机构——就像2008年末多国政府（尤其是美国）采取的救市举措；政府也无法采购必要物资、发放薪酬维持公共运转，最终丧失治理权威。
A classic sign of Stage 5 is when large government deficits lead to government debt issuance exceeding the willingness of buyers other than the government's own central bank to buy.
第五阶段的典型特征：政府巨额赤字推高发债规模，除本国央行外，外部市场投资者不再愿意接盘国债。
When governments that cannot print money have to raise taxes and cut spending, or governments that can print money print a lot and buy a lot of government bonds, this leading indicator is triggered.

无法自主印钞的国家被迫加税、削减公共开支；拥有货币发行权的国家则大举印钞、自购国债，出现以上任意一种情况，都意味着该风险指标已经触发。
---

More specifically, when a government faces large deficits, large debts, and an inability to get sufficient credit, its options are very limited. It can either raise taxes and cut spending sharply or print a lot of money, which leads to currency devaluation.
具体而言，当政府深陷高额赤字、巨额债务，且难以获得外部信贷时，可选择的应对方式少之又少：要么大幅加税、削减开支，要么大量印钞——而印钞必然会引发货币贬值。
Governments that can print money always do so because it is the least painful path, but this leads to investors dumping the money and debt created by the printing.
拥有铸币权的政府往往会选择印钞，因为这是短期代价最小的方式，但此举会引发投资者抛售本币与本国债券。
Governments that cannot print money have to raise taxes and cut spending, which forces people with money to flee the country because paying more taxes becomes unbearable.
没有铸币权的国家只能选择加税、节流，过重的税负会迫使富裕人群携资产外流。
Tax increases and service reductions are intolerable. If these unprintable jurisdictions have large wealth gaps, these moves usually lead to some form of civil war/revolution.

税负上涨、公共服务缩水会引发民众强烈不满。若这类地区同时存在巨大贫富差距，相关举措极易诱发内战或革命。
---
Areas (cities, states, and countries) with the largest wealth gaps, highest debts, and worst income declines are the most prone to conflict.
贫富差距越大、债务负担越重、居民收入下滑越明显的地区（城市、州、国家），爆发冲突的概率就越高。

Interestingly, the U.S. states and cities with the highest per capita income and wealth levels are often the ones with the most debt and the largest wealth gaps—cities like San Francisco, Chicago, and New York City, and states like Connecticut, Illinois, Massachusetts, New York, and New Jersey.
一个值得关注的现象是：美国人均收入和财富排名靠前的州与城市，往往也是债务最高、贫富差距最悬殊的区域，例如旧金山、芝加哥、纽约等城市，以及康涅狄格州、伊利诺伊州、马萨诸塞州、纽约州、新泽西州。
Faced with these conditions, you either cut spending or find ways to raise more money. The next question is who will bear the cost of solving these problems—the rich or the poor?
面对这样的困境，政府无非两条路：削减开支，或是开辟新财源。而核心矛盾随之而来：解决危机的成本，最终该由富人承担，还是由穷人承担？

Obviously, the poor cannot afford it. Spending cuts are most unbearable for the poorest, so tax increases on those who can afford to pay more are needed, but this increases the risk of some form of civil war or revolution.

显然，穷人无力承担额外成本。削减公共开支对底层民众的冲击最大，因此政府只能向高收入群体加税，但这一做法会进一步激化矛盾，提升内战或革命的风险。
---

Another feature of Stage 5 is the emergence of populism and extremism. I point out that chaos and dissatisfaction give rise to charismatic, anti-elitist leaders who claim to fight for the common people. They are called populists.
第五阶段的另一大特征，是民粹主义与极端主义抬头。社会动荡与民众不满，会催生一批富有号召力、反对精英阶层的领袖，他们宣称要为普通民众发声，这便是民粹主义者。
Populism is a political and social phenomenon that caters to ordinary people who feel their demands are not being addressed by the elite.
民粹主义是一种政治与社会现象，它精准迎合了那些诉求长期被精英阶层忽视的普通民众。

It usually develops when there are gaps in wealth and opportunity, cultural threats from different value groups at home and abroad, and "establishment elites" in power who fail to effectively serve most people.
当社会出现财富与机会分配不均、国内外不同价值观群体产生文化对立，且掌权的建制派精英无法服务大多数民众时，民粹主义就会快速发展。
When these conditions arouse the anger of ordinary people who want those in political power to fight for them, populists come to power.

当种种问题激起民愤，民众迫切希望掌权者为自己争取权益时，民粹主义者便会借机上台。
---
Populists can be right-wing or left-wing, more extreme than moderates, and tend to appeal to the emotions of ordinary people.
民粹主义者既有右翼也有左翼，立场远比武派人士激进，且擅长煽动民众情绪。
They are usually confrontational rather than cooperative, exclusive rather than inclusive. This leads to bitter conflicts between left-wing and right-wing populists over irreconcilable differences.
他们处事风格偏向对抗而非合作，立场偏向排外而非包容。左右两翼的民粹主义者因理念无法调和，会爆发激烈对抗。
A typical feature of Stage 5, and a prominent feature of Stage 6, is the demonization of other classes.
将其他阶层“妖魔化”，是第五阶段的典型表现，更是第六阶段的突出特征。
This demonization usually creates one or more scapegoat classes that are widely blamed for being the source of problems.
这种妖魔化行为，往往会塑造出一个或多个“替罪阶层”，全社会将所有问题都归咎于他们。
This leads to impulses to exclude, imprison, or eliminate them, which emerge in Stage 6. Racial, ethnic, and socioeconomic groups are often demonized.
到了第六阶段，社会会滋生出排斥、拘禁甚至清除这些群体的想法。种族、族群以及不同社会经济阶层，常常会沦为被妖魔化的对象。
The most classic and horrific example is the Nazi persecution of Jews, who were blamed for almost all of Germany's problems and persecuted as a result.
最典型也最惨烈的例子，就是纳粹对犹太人的迫害。当时德国将国内所有问题都归咎于犹太人，并对其展开残酷打压。

In Stage 5, there is also a loss of truth in the public sphere. I show that at this time, due to distortions by media and propaganda, it becomes increasingly difficult for people to distinguish truth, which leads to people's positions becoming increasingly polarized, emotional, and politically motivated.
第五阶段还会出现公共领域真相缺失的问题。受媒体歪曲与舆论宣传影响，民众越来越难分辨事实，立场随之不断两极分化，看待问题愈发情绪化、政治化。

In times of large wealth gaps and populist popularity, stories exposing the downfall of elites are often both popular and profitable—especially stories exposing left-wing elites in right-wing media and right-wing elites in left-wing media.

在贫富差距悬殊、民粹主义盛行的时期，曝光精英阶层丑闻的内容往往流量与收益双高。右翼媒体专攻左翼精英，左翼媒体紧盯右翼精英，相互攻伐成为常态。
---

Two classic signs of the transition from Stage 5 to Stage 6 seem to be emerging: (1) "People dying in conflicts almost certainly marks the development to the next more violent civil war stage, which will continue until a clear winner emerges" and (2) "History shows that during major conflicts, federal democracies (like the U.S.) usually experience conflicts between states and the central government over their respective powers."
目前，两大标志性迹象已经出现，预示社会正从第五阶段向第六阶段过渡：第一，冲突出现人员伤亡，基本意味着局势会滑向暴力程度更高的内战阶段，且对抗会持续到分出胜负为止；第二，历史规律显示，在大规模冲突期间，美国这类联邦制民主国家，常会爆发州政府与联邦政府的权力之争。
The U.S. is now a tinderbox. According to the latest PBS News/NPR/Marist poll, nearly one-third of Americans (30%) believe that people may have to resort to violence to get the country back on track.
如今的美国就像一个火药桶。美国公共广播公司、国家公共广播电台联合马里斯特学院的最新民调显示，近三成（30%）美国人认为，想要让国家重回正轨，民众或许不得不诉诸暴力。
A Pew Research Center survey (September-October 2025) found that 85% of U.S. adults acknowledge that political violence is increasing in the United States.
皮尤研究中心2025年9至10月的调查显示，85%的美国成年人承认，美国境内的政治性暴力事件正在不断增多。

An analysis by the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) shows that from 2016 to 2024, there were 21 partisan political attacks or plots, compared to only two such incidents in the more than 25 years before 2016.
战略与国际研究中心的分析数据显示：2016至2024年间，美国共发生21起带有党派色彩的政治袭击与阴谋事件；而在2016年之前的25年多时间里，同类事件仅发生过两起。
This means that in a relatively short period, politically motivated plots/attacks increased about tenfold.
这意味着在短短数年里，政治性袭击与阴谋事件的数量暴涨了近十倍。
There are more guns than people in the U.S., and many are inclined toward violence.
美国的枪支保有量已经超过总人口数量，不少民众也逐渐滋生暴力倾向。
There is no doubt that the conflict between the central government and Minnesota (and other state governments) is very serious and looks likely to worsen.
联邦政府与明尼苏达州及其他部分州政府之间的矛盾已十分尖锐，且大概率会进一步升级。
The world has seen the killings of two opponents of Trump's ICE program in Minneapolis and is watching to see which side will back down.

全球都关注着明尼阿波利斯事件：两名反对特朗普移民执法政策的人士遇害，各方都在观望对峙双方谁会率先让步。
---

Many are waiting to see whether President Trump will continue to fight—which I believe risks pushing us closer to the edge of clearer civil war—or whether he will try to pull us back from the brink by calling for peace, promising and showing that the justice system will properly handle the shootings, and limiting ICE activities.
很多人都在观望特朗普总统的选择：如果他选择继续强硬对抗，我认为这会将美国进一步推向全面内战的边缘；如果他呼吁各方保持克制、承诺司法部门会公正处理枪击案件、同时收紧移民执法行动，则有望将国家从危机边缘拉回。

While President Trump's choices will have a huge impact on what happens next and may even light the fuse, it is important to view everything that is happening in the context of the various forces and events driving the "Big Cycle."
特朗普的决策会深刻影响短期局势，甚至可能成为冲突的导火索。但我们必须明白，所有事件都要放在推动“大周期”演变的深层力量中去审视。
Regardless of how the Minneapolis incident ultimately turns out, these major forces that are evolving and determining the direction of the "Big Cycle" are what matter most.

无论明尼阿波利斯事件最终如何收场，真正决定未来走向的，是那些推动大周期演进的核心深层力量。
---
Money and credit are the lifeblood of every economy, and they are inseparable from the political and social cycles I have described above.
货币与信贷是所有经济体的命脉，它和前文提到的政治、社会周期紧密相连、无法分割。

Throughout history, every dominant reserve currency has followed the same long-term cycle: it rises alongside a rising empire, thrives during its peak power, and then declines as the empire loses strength, fiscal discipline breaks down, and internal conflicts grow.
纵观历史，每一种主导性储备货币都遵循相同的长期周期：它随强国崛起而兴盛，在国家实力顶峰时达到巅峰，又会随着国力衰退、财政秩序崩坏、内部冲突加剧而逐步走弱。
The U.S. dollar became the world’s primary reserve currency after World War II, built on America’s economic, military, and geopolitical dominance at that time.
二战后，依托当时美国在经济、军事与地缘政治上的绝对优势，美元成为全球首要储备货币。

Today, the United States faces the same fiscal troubles that ended the reign of previous reserve currencies: persistent large deficits, unsustainable national debt, and a growing need to monetize debt to keep the system afloat.
如今，美国正遭遇昔日各大储备货币霸权终结时的同类困境：长期高额财政赤字、难以为继的国债规模，并且越来越依赖债务货币化来维持体系运转。

Monetizing debt means the central bank prints money to buy government debt. This temporarily lowers borrowing costs and prevents an immediate crisis, but it erodes the value of the currency over time and fuels inflation.
债务货币化，即央行印钞购入本国国债。这种方式能暂时压低融资成本、化解短期危机，但长期会不断侵蚀货币信用，推高通胀。

When a currency loses trust globally, countries begin to diversify their reserves away from it. Trade settlements shift to other currencies, and capital flows change direction. This is a slow but irreversible process once it gains momentum.
当一种货币失去全球信任，各国就会开始减持该货币储备，国际贸易结算也会转向其他币种，资本流向随之改变。这一过程一旦启动，虽进展缓慢，但趋势难以逆转。
We are now seeing clear signs of dollar diversification across the globe. This does not mean the dollar will disappear overnight, but its dominance will gradually weaken over the next decade or two.
当前全球范围内，去美元化、外汇储备多元化的迹象已经十分明显。这并不代表美元会立刻失去地位，但在未来一二十年里，它的主导影响力会逐步下滑。
Weakening currency power worsens domestic social tensions. Higher inflation hits low-income families hardest, widening the wealth gap further and feeding the anger that drives populism and conflict.
货币地位走弱会进一步加剧国内社会矛盾。通胀高企对低收入家庭打击最大，贫富差距持续拉大，民众不满情绪不断积累，反过来又助长民粹主义与各类冲突。
In short, domestic fiscal decline, currency devaluation and social unrest form a self-reinforcing downward spiral. This spiral is a core part of the late Stage 5 and early Stage 6 of the Big Cycle.

简言之，财政恶化、货币贬值、社会动荡三者会形成恶性循环。而这一循环，正是大周期第五阶段末期、第六阶段初期的核心特征。
---

History repeatedly shows that severe internal divisions and civil strife within major powers rarely stay contained inside national borders. They often spill over into international conflicts and full-scale wars.
历史反复印证：大国深陷严重内部分裂与内乱时，冲突几乎不会局限在国境之内，往往会向外蔓延，演变为国际对抗乃至全面战争。

There are two main reasons for this pattern. First, leaders facing domestic unrest often use external enemies to unify their divided populations. Creating an external threat is a common tool to divert public attention from domestic problems.
这一规律主要有两大成因。第一，当执政者面临国内动荡时，常会树立外部“敌人”来凝聚分裂的国民。制造外部威胁，是转移民众对国内矛盾注意力的常用手段。

Second, when a dominant world power is in decline, rival powers will take advantage of its internal weakness to challenge its global position. Power vacuums always lead to competition and fighting for influence.
第二，当全球主导大国走向衰落时，竞争对手会利用其内部乱象，趁机挑战其国际地位。权力真空一旦出现，必然会引发各方势力争夺影响力。

The period between 1930 and 1945 is the clearest modern example. Major nations all suffered from severe domestic economic crises, wealth gaps, political polarization and civil tensions. Those internal problems eventually merged into a global world war.
1930至1945年就是近代最鲜明的例证：当时各大强国普遍遭遇经济危机、贫富分化、政治对立与内部矛盾，这些国内问题最终交织在一起，演变为世界大战。
Today, major global powers are simultaneously moving through similar late-cycle stages. They face heavy debt, fiscal stress, social division and weakening currency credibility at the same time.
如今，全球主要大国几乎同步步入周期尾声阶段，普遍背负高额债务、承受财政压力、遭遇社会分裂，货币信用也持续走弱。

Geopolitical competition has already intensified across multiple regions. Trade tensions, technological decoupling, diplomatic confrontations and regional military standoffs are all signs of rising international risk.
多地地缘博弈已然升级：贸易摩擦、技术脱钩、外交对峙、地区军事僵持，都预示着国际冲突风险不断上升。

Civil war at home and war abroad are not separate events. They are two sides of the same cycle of declining order. The same pressures that tear societies apart internally also push nations toward conflict with one another.

国内内战与国际战争并非彼此孤立，而是秩序崩塌周期的一体两面。那些撕裂社会的内部压力，同样会推动国与国之间走向对抗。
---
I have studied dozens of countries that went through this full cycle over the past 500 years. The playbook is nearly identical across different cultures, regions and eras.
在过去500年里，我研究了数十个走完完整大周期的国家。抛开文化、地域与时代差异，它们的演变轨迹几乎如出一辙。

European powers in the 17th and 18th centuries, the British Empire in the early 20th century, and many smaller regional powers all followed this path: prosperity → excess → fiscal trouble → class conflict → internal violence → external war.
17至18世纪的欧洲列强、20世纪初的大英帝国，以及众多区域性小国，都走过同一条路：繁荣鼎盛→奢靡过剩→财政危机→阶级对抗→内部暴力冲突→对外战争。

One common mistake leaders make is believing that "it cannot happen here." Every society believes it is uniquely immune to the cycles that destroyed past civilizations. This overconfidence makes them unprepared.
各国执政者常会陷入一个误区：认为“灾难不会降临到自己身上”。每一个社会都自以为能独善其身，不会重蹈昔日文明的覆辙。而这种过度自信，会让整个社会丧失应对风险的准备。

Even countries with strong institutions and long histories of stability eventually break down when the combination of unsustainable debt, huge wealth gaps and lost trust in government lasts for too long.
即便是制度完善、长期稳定的国家，若高额债务、贫富悬殊、政府公信力缺失的状态长期延续，最终也难逃秩序崩塌的结局。
Recent decades have given us a long stretch of relative peace and stability. Many people have grown up knowing nothing else, so they cannot imagine radical change and large-scale conflict.

过去数十年全球整体处于相对和平稳定的状态，几代人都生长在这样的环境中，因此很难想象剧烈变革与大规模冲突会到来。
---
Based on all these trends, I see three plausible paths for the coming 5 to 10 years. None of them are easy, but they differ greatly in severity.
综合以上所有趋势判断，我认为未来5至10年大概率会出现三种发展路径。三条路径都充满挑战，但危机严重程度差异巨大。

First path: Managed decline and gradual reform. Governments make tough but necessary fiscal reforms, slow down debt growth, narrow wealth gaps through reasonable policy adjustments, and de-escalate political and geopolitical tensions. This is the best possible outcome.
第一种路径：有序衰退+渐进改革。各国政府推行必要且强硬的财政改革，控制债务增速，通过合理政策缩小贫富差距，同时缓和国内政治对立与国际地缘矛盾。这是最理想的结果。

Second path: Long-term stagnation and recurring small conflicts. Fiscal problems remain unsolved, wealth gaps stay wide, and social polarization continues. We see frequent small-scale civil unrest, periodic geopolitical frictions, and slow currency decline. No full-scale war or civil war, but constant instability.
第二种路径：长期停滞+零星冲突。财政顽疾无法根治，贫富差距居高不下，社会两极分化持续加剧。社会层面频发小规模骚乱，国际层面摩擦不断，货币缓慢贬值。不会爆发全面内战或世界大战，但整个世界将长期处于动荡之中。

Third path: Full escalation into major civil conflict and international war. This happens when political compromise completely breaks down, violence becomes normalized domestically, and great power rivalry turns into open military conflict. This is the most destructive scenario.
第三种路径：局势全面升级，爆发大规模内战与国际战争。当政治妥协彻底失效、暴力成为国内常态、大国博弈演变为正面军事对抗时，就会走向这一结局，也是破坏力最强的情景。

At present, the momentum is leaning toward the second path. But single major events—like the Minneapolis violence or miscalculations between major powers—could push us toward the third path very quickly.

目前局势的发展趋势偏向第二种路径。但明尼阿波利斯暴力事件这类突发事件，或是大国之间的战略误判，都可能让局势迅速滑向第三种最坏情景。
---

Building productive win-win relationships through skilled cooperation that both expands the pie and distributes it well so that most people are satisfied is more meaningful and far less painful than fighting a civil war over wealth and power that results in one side conquering the other.
通过务实合作构建互利共赢的关系，把社会财富这块“蛋糕”做大，同时做好分配，让大多数人安居乐业，这远比为了财富与权力大打内战、最终走向一方碾压另一方的结局更有意义，代价也小得多。
The same logic applies to international relations. Competition between nations is inevitable, but destructive war is not. Cooperation and fair competition can replace conflict.
这一道理同样适用于国际关系。国与国之间的竞争无法避免，但毁灭性的战争并非必然。合作与公平竞争，完全可以取代对抗。
Understanding the big cycles does not mean we have to accept a tragic fate. Recognizing the patterns is the first step to changing the outcome.
认清大周期的规律，不代表我们只能被动接受悲剧结局。看懂历史轨迹，正是扭转局势的第一步。
We now stand at a critical turning point. The choices made by leaders and ordinary people around the world in the next few years will write the next chapter of history.
我们如今正站在关键的历史转折点。未来数年，全球各国决策者与普通民众的选择，将会书写下一段全新的历史。
I write this analysis not to predict doom, but to encourage awareness, preparation, and rational action before it is too late.

我撰写这篇分析，并非为了渲染悲观论调，而是希望唤醒人们的认知，提醒大家在为时已晚之前做好准备、理性行事。

The Fed's shift from balance sheet reduction to expansion signals dangerous late-cycle debt dynamics. While being framed as a technical adjustment, it has the same economic effect as monetary easing, and it comes at a time when markets, debt, and valuations are already overheated. This is a classic Big Debt Cycle pattern: governments accumulate debt, resort to money printing, and fuel bubbles that eventually burst.
